prompt:
Correct the ANATOMY of the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL CULLER. It wrongly has only FOUR ground-support legs plus two scythes. The intended machine is a true SIX-LEGGED industrial HEXAPOD, PLUS TWO separate front scythe tool arms. ADD THE MISSING MIDDLE PAIR OF DRIVE LEGS on independent middle hip joints. There must be EIGHT appendages total: SIX locomotive legs ending in six small FLAT PLANT FOOT PADS (three left, three right) AND TWO non-support curved SCYTHE ARMS on front servo shoulders, whose blade tips never count as feet.

Keep the same low long plated industrial chassis, dark gunmetal/bronze/olive ageing, compact front sensor face, closed rectangular net-spool case, single side purification-fluid tank, passive rear cooling louvres and closed internal core hatch. No exposed glowing reactor or organic insect anatomy, no weapon held by humanoid hands. Longer chassis/spacing is allowed to fit three distinct hip pairs. All SIX feet must be countable in every sprite: in elevated SIDE views draw three near legs with separated feet along body front/middle/rear and expose the three far foot pads slightly offset beyond them; in FRONT/BACK views use perspective to separate three foot pads down each side of chassis, not collapse them to two. None of the six drive legs ends in a scythe blade.

Transparent RGBA sprite atlas, exactly FOUR ROWS x FOUR COLUMNS. Rows FRONT toward bottom, LEFT front left, RIGHT front right, BACK front away to top, four distinct subtle idle sensor/blade-servo adjustments per row. All supporting feet grounded, no walking/slashing/firing effects. Keep scale/camera/component count stable. VERY LARGE transparent gutters: miniature robots only central 50 percent of each cell, no neighbor rectangular crop overlap, no outer-edge clipping. No floor/shadow/grid/text/labels/checkerboard. Detailed crisp pixel-art clusters and complete body in every cell. Main priority: SIX separate ground-contact foot pads plus TWO separate curved scythe arms, not the current four-leg anatomy.
